rows.reason: The tick runs on Claude Code's `loop` skill exactly as upstream writes it on a terminal root: `/loop 1h <prompt>` is the fixed-interval form (a `CronCreate` entry of the session), which Claude Code restores on `--resume` and ends after 7 days (measured on 2.1.289, 2026-10-05), and which a terminal root delivers on time with background tasks alive (measured on 2.1.293, 2026-10-08). A root inside the Claude desktop app cannot use it: that host delivers a scheduled prompt only at the first turn end with no background task alive, and a program always has background owners (same measurement), so SKILL.md's Platform Adaptation names its cadence, a background `Bash` command that sleeps an hour and prints the tick prompt, re-armed by each tick. Upstream's sentence about local and cloud roots names Cursor's cloud agents; the port's root is a local session, and the sentence becomes the pointer to the other cadences: Codex has no `loop` skill and codex-tools.md names its cadence (native heartbeat on the exact root thread when supported, otherwise finite CLI events explicitly rearmed by a local controller with the thread loaded in a running host, and the operator's hourly re-prompt only when neither mechanism is valid), a Grok root arms a monitor ticker per grok-tools.md, and a desktop-app Claude root follows SKILL.md.
